summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 100-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts barely moves (mostly under 30 views). The best video, the PIR motion sensor one, got about 1,400 Instagram views and 529 YouTube views, far above the rest. The only English video did better on YouTube (157) than most Hindi ones, but it has no Instagram numbers, so the data is too thin to say language is the problem. Shares and saves are very low everywhere, so viewers watch but rarely act.
winningPattern: Everyday device or sensor people meet daily (motion sensor, street light, phone orientation) + a curiosity hook that flips an assumption ('Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', 'Kaise Pata Chalta Hai?') + Hinglish question title with 🤔 and #shorts, posted mainly on Instagram Reels. The top video also has a surprising claim in the title, which the weaker ones lack.
doMore: Lead titles and first lines with a surprising claim or myth-flip, like the PIR video, instead of a plain 'how does X work' question
Pick familiar devices people touch daily (lift sensor, fridge door, ATM, fan regulator, AC remote) over abstract modules
Treat Instagram as the main platform and test YouTube separately with a few English or bilingual titles, since the Arduino Uno video got 157 views there
End each video with a save or share prompt such as 'Save karo exam ke liye' or 'Dost ko bhejo jo yeh sochta hai', since saves and shares are near zero
Post on a steady schedule and compare same-topic videos across a week before judging a format, as most videos are only 1-6 days old
stopDoing: Judging YouTube performance from Hindi titles alone; test, don't assume
Plain neutral titles with no surprise (Smartwatch, Smoke Detector, Mall Door got little reaction)
Reading too much into single videos with a few days of data
